declared.title: The Cantril Ladder elicits thoughts about power and wealth
declared.foundIn: counter-evidence report reports/money-happiness/counter-evidence.md; OpenAlex search « The Cantril Ladder elicits thoughts about power and wealth » (2026-11-22)

population: 1,581 UK adults randomly given different framings of the life-evaluation ladder

findings.text: The ladder question most surveys use makes people think of power and wealth more than other framings do

support.sentence: Using three language analysis techniques (dictionary, topic, and word embeddings), we found that the Cantril Ladder framing emphasizes power and wealth over broader well-being and relationship concepts in comparison to the other study conditions.

limits: one UK study of word associations: it does not measure how much this inflates the income link
a risk of bias for the life-evaluation evidence, not evidence on money itself
